Abaqus 2024 Scripting Reference
High-Quality Sample Scripts by Category
This document contains 26 self-contained Abaqus 2024 Python scripting patterns, retrieved by Consultant and
Coding Agent as example patterns for common scripting operations -- NOT an exhaustive API reference, and not
a substitute for official Abaqus/SIMULIA documentation.
On correctness: every script below has been validated for Python SYNTAX correctness (parsed without error).
They have NOT been executed against a live Abaqus installation, and API-level correctness (correct method
names, correct argument names/types for the current Abaqus 2024 release) reflects careful, well-established
knowledge of the Abaqus scripting API rather than live verification. Spot-check a sample against a real Abaqus
install before treating this set as fully verified.
On named regions: many scripts below operate on a named set, surface, or region (e.g. SET_NAME,
SURFACE_NAME). Every such script explicitly checks that the named region already exists before proceeding,
and raises a clear error if it does not. NEVER remove this check, and NEVER replace a missing named region
with a programmatically guessed geometric selection (coordinate-based, bounding-box, or otherwise) -- if the
required region does not exist in the model, that is a genuine gap that needs to be resolved upstream (the region
must be defined in the model itself), not something a script should work around silently.
Template used for every script below: Title & Category, Description, Prerequisites/Assumptions, Inputs
Required, Key API Objects/Methods, the Script itself, and Notes/Caveats.

1. Import STEP Geometry and Create a Part
Category: Part / Geometry
Description
Imports raw CAD geometry from a .step/.stp file and creates a corresponding Abaqus part. This is the starting
point for any task that begins from uploaded CAD geometry.
Prerequisites / Assumptions
A valid .step or .stp file must exist at STEP_FILE_PATH.
Inputs Required

MODEL_NAME (str): Name for the model database entry, e.g. "Model-1"

STEP_FILE_PATH (str): Absolute path to the .step/.stp file

PART_NAME (str): Name to assign to the imported part
Key API Objects / Methods Used
mdb.openStep(), model.PartFromGeometryFile()
Script
from abaqus import mdb
import abaqusConstants as C
 
# === USER INPUTS ===
MODEL_NAME = "Model-1"
STEP_FILE_PATH = "/path/to/geometry.stp"
PART_NAME = "ImportedPart"
# ====================
 
model = mdb.models[MODEL_NAME]
 
step_import = mdb.openStep(STEP_FILE_PATH, scaleFromFile=C.OFF)
model.PartFromGeometryFile(
    name=PART_NAME,
    geometryFile=step_import,
    combine=False,
    dimensionality=C.THREE_D,
    type=C.DEFORMABLE_BODY,
)
 
print("Imported STEP geometry from '{}' and created part '{}'".format(STEP_FILE_PATH, PART_
NAME))
Notes / Caveats
PERSISTENCE: this script assumes MODEL_NAME's default fresh model (auto-created when a new mdb
session starts) -- there is nothing to open from an existing .inp yet at this stage. If this is the ONLY operation in
this script's dispatch, add a final job.writeInput() call (see the Write an Updated Input File script) to persist the
imported part before this process ends -- otherwise, if instancing/meshing continue in the SAME script (the typical
case), only write out the .inp ONCE, at the true end of the combined script, not after every individual sub-step.

2. Isotropic Elastic Material and Whole-Part Solid Section
Category: Materials & Sections
Description
Opens an existing model from its .inp file, creates a simple isotropic elastic material and a matching
homogeneous solid section, assigns that section to an entire part, and writes the updated model back out to a
new .inp. Use this when the whole part is a single material.
Prerequisites / Assumptions
INP_FILE_PATH must point to a valid, existing .inp file already containing the part PART_NAME with solid (3D)
geometry.
Inputs Required

INP_FILE_PATH (str): Absolute path to the existing .inp file to open

WORKING_DIRECTORY (str): The task's working directory -- all output must land here, and nowhere else

MODEL_NAME (str): Name to assign the model reconstructed from the .inp

PART_NAME (str): Name of the part to assign the section to (confirm this against the actual model -- see the
List All Defined Sets utility script if uncertain)

MATERIAL_NAME (str): Name for the new material, e.g. "Steel"

YOUNGS_MODULUS (float): Young's modulus, in consistent units (e.g. MPa)

POISSONS_RATIO (float): Poisson's ratio

SECTION_NAME (str): Name for the new solid section

OUTPUT_JOB_NAME (str): Name used to write the updated model as OUTPUT_JOB_NAME.inp
Key API Objects / Methods Used
mdb.ModelFromInputFile(), model.Material(), model.HomogeneousSolidSection(), part.Set(),
part.SectionAssignment(), job.writeInput()
Script
from abaqus import mdb
import os
 
# === USER INPUTS ===
INP_FILE_PATH = "/path/to/working_directory/current_model.inp"
WORKING_DIRECTORY = "/path/to/working_directory"
MODEL_NAME = "ImportedModel"
PART_NAME = "Part-1"
MATERIAL_NAME = "Steel"
YOUNGS_MODULUS = 200000.0  # MPa
POISSONS_RATIO = 0.3
SECTION_NAME = "Solid-Section-1"
OUTPUT_JOB_NAME = "UpdatedModel"
# ====================
 
# All implicit-path Abaqus writes (job.writeInput()) use the process's
# current working directory -- there is no path argument for this call.
# Change into WORKING_DIRECTORY before any such call so output lands where
# it must, per the standing rule that every output goes inside
# WORKING_DIRECTORY and nowhere else.
os.chdir(WORKING_DIRECTORY)

Source: abaqus_2024_scripting_reference.pdf
Page: 5

# Guard against silently overwriting the very file this script just opened.
if OUTPUT_JOB_NAME + ".inp" == os.path.basename(INP_FILE_PATH):
    raise ValueError(
        "OUTPUT_JOB_NAME ('{}.inp') matches the input file's name -- choose a "
        "distinct output name to avoid overwriting the original file.".format(OUTPUT_JOB_NA
ME)
    )
 
mdb.ModelFromInputFile(name=MODEL_NAME, inputFileName=INP_FILE_PATH)
model = mdb.models[MODEL_NAME]
part = model.parts[PART_NAME]
 
material = model.Material(name=MATERIAL_NAME)
material.Elastic(table=((YOUNGS_MODULUS, POISSONS_RATIO),))
 
model.HomogeneousSolidSection(name=SECTION_NAME, material=MATERIAL_NAME)
 
all_cells = part.cells[:]
region = part.Set(cells=all_cells, name="WholePart-Set")
part.SectionAssignment(region=region, sectionName=SECTION_NAME)
 
# Persist the updated model -- this process's in-memory model does not
# survive once this script finishes; a later, separately-dispatched script
# must be able to pick up from here.
export_job = mdb.Job(name=OUTPUT_JOB_NAME, model=MODEL_NAME)
export_job.writeInput(consistencyChecking=False)
 
print("Assigned material '{}' via section '{}' to entire part '{}'. Wrote updated model to 
'{}.inp'".format(
    MATERIAL_NAME, SECTION_NAME, PART_NAME, OUTPUT_JOB_NAME
))
Notes / Caveats
If the part is shell/2D geometry rather than solid, use faces instead of cells when building the Set. The exact
PART_NAME after ModelFromInputFile depends on how the original .inp was authored -- confirm it via the List
All Defined Sets utility script if it's not already known.
3. Region-Specific Material and Section Assignment
Category: Materials & Sections
Description
Opens an existing model, assigns a material and section to only a specific named region of a part (rather than the
whole part), and persists the result -- for tasks like "the hub should be aluminum, the shaft should be steel" where
both are modeled as one part.
Prerequisites / Assumptions
INP_FILE_PATH must point to a valid, existing .inp file. SET_NAME must already exist as a defined set on the
part. This script does NOT invent, guess, or programmatically derive this set -- it checks for its existence and
raises an error if not found.
Inputs Required

4. Shell Section with Thickness
Category: Materials & Sections
Description
Opens an existing model, creates an isotropic elastic material and a homogeneous shell section with a specified
thickness, assigns it to an entire shell part, and persists the result.
Prerequisites / Assumptions
INP_FILE_PATH must point to a valid, existing .inp file already containing the part PART_NAME with shell (2D
surface) geometry.
Inputs Required

INP_FILE_PATH (str): Absolute path to the existing .inp file to open

WORKING_DIRECTORY (str): The task's working directory -- all output must land here, and nowhere else

MODEL_NAME (str): Name to assign the model reconstructed from the .inp

PART_NAME (str): Name of the shell part

MATERIAL_NAME (str): Name for the new material

YOUNGS_MODULUS (float): Young's modulus, in consistent units

POISSONS_RATIO (float): Poisson's ratio

SECTION_NAME (str): Name for the new shell section

THICKNESS (float): Shell thickness, in consistent units (e.g. mm)

5. Create a Part Instance
Category: Assembly
Description
Creates an instance of a part in the root assembly, as either dependent (mesh comes from the part) or
independent (instance has its own mesh).
Prerequisites / Assumptions
The part PART_NAME must already exist in the CURRENT session (typically just created via the STEP import
script, in the SAME script) -- an .inp file already contains its own assembly/instance definitions, so this script is
not meant to resume from an existing .inp.
Inputs Required

MODEL_NAME (str): Name of the model database entry (matching whatever the geometry-import step used)

PART_NAME (str): Name of the part to instance

INSTANCE_NAME (str): Name for the new instance

DEPENDENT (bool): True for a dependent instance, False for independent
Key API Objects / Methods Used
assembly.Instance()
Script
from abaqus import mdb
import abaqusConstants as C
 
# === USER INPUTS ===
MODEL_NAME = "Model-1"
PART_NAME = "Part-1"
INSTANCE_NAME = "Part-1-1"
DEPENDENT = True
# ====================
 
model = mdb.models[MODEL_NAME]
assembly = model.rootAssembly
part = model.parts[PART_NAME]
 
dependent_flag = C.ON if DEPENDENT else C.OFF
assembly.Instance(name=INSTANCE_NAME, part=part, dependent=dependent_flag)
 
print("Created instance '{}' of part '{}' ({})".format(
    INSTANCE_NAME, PART_NAME, "dependent" if DEPENDENT else "independent"
))
Notes / Caveats
PERSISTENCE: same as the STEP import script -- if this is the last operation in its dispatch, add a final
job.writeInput() (see the Write an Updated Input File script) before this process ends. If meshing continues in the
same script, write out only once, at the true end.

6. Global Seed and Mesh a Whole Part
Category: Mesh
Description
Applies a uniform global seed size to an entire part and generates the mesh. Use this when meshing applies
uniformly across the whole part, with no region-specific refinement.
Prerequisites / Assumptions
The part PART_NAME must already exist in the CURRENT session with native CAD geometry (from a STEP
import, in the SAME script) -- NOT reconstructed from a plain .inp file. A typical .inp is already a mesh-based
solver format and generally has no native geometry for Abaqus's meshing tools to operate on; this script is for the
geometry-import stage, before any .inp has been written for this model.
Inputs Required

MODEL_NAME (str): Name of the model database entry (matching whatever the geometry-import step used)

PART_NAME (str): Name of the part to mesh

GLOBAL_SEED_SIZE (float): Approximate global element size, in consistent units
Key API Objects / Methods Used
part.seedPart(), part.generateMesh()
Script
from abaqus import mdb
 
# === USER INPUTS ===
MODEL_NAME = "Model-1"
PART_NAME = "Part-1"
GLOBAL_SEED_SIZE = 5.0
# ====================
 
model = mdb.models[MODEL_NAME]
part = model.parts[PART_NAME]
 
part.seedPart(size=GLOBAL_SEED_SIZE, deviationFactor=0.1, minSizeFactor=0.1)
part.generateMesh()
 
num_elements = len(part.elements)
print("Meshed part '{}' with global seed size {} -- {} elements generated".format(
    PART_NAME, GLOBAL_SEED_SIZE, num_elements
))
Notes / Caveats
PERSISTENCE: meshing is typically the natural checkpoint at the end of the geometry-import stage -- once
meshed, add a final job.writeInput() (see the Write an Updated Input File script) to persist the meshed model to
.inp, so later, separately-dispatched scripts (materials, loads, etc.) can open it from there. If generateMesh()
completes without error but len(part.elements) is 0, the geometry likely has an unmeshable topology -- surface
this as a genuine failure, not a silent success.
7. Region-Specific Local Seed and Mesh Refinement
Category: Mesh

Source: abaqus_2024_scripting_reference.pdf
Page: 12

Description
Applies a finer local seed to a specific named edge set, in addition to a coarser global seed, then meshes the
part. Use this for tasks like "refine the mesh near the fillet".
Prerequisites / Assumptions
Same as the global-mesh script: the part must exist in the CURRENT session with native geometry, not
reconstructed from a plain .inp. EDGE_SET_NAME must already exist as a defined set of edges on the part.
Inputs Required

MODEL_NAME (str): Name of the model database entry

PART_NAME (str): Name of the part to mesh

EDGE_SET_NAME (str): The exact, pre-existing edge set name for local refinement

LOCAL_SEED_SIZE (float): Local element size at the refined region

GLOBAL_SEED_SIZE (float): Global element size elsewhere on the part
Key API Objects / Methods Used
part.seedPart(), part.seedEdgeBySize(), part.generateMesh()
Script
from abaqus import mdb
import abaqusConstants as C
 
# === USER INPUTS ===
MODEL_NAME = "Model-1"
PART_NAME = "Part-1"
EDGE_SET_NAME = "Fillet-Edges"
LOCAL_SEED_SIZE = 1.0
GLOBAL_SEED_SIZE = 5.0
# ====================
 
model = mdb.models[MODEL_NAME]
part = model.parts[PART_NAME]
 
# This script assumes EDGE_SET_NAME already exists as a defined set of edges
# on the part. It does not invent or guess this name -- confirm it exists
# before running this script.
if EDGE_SET_NAME not in part.sets.keys():
    raise ValueError("Set '{}' does not exist on part '{}'.".format(EDGE_SET_NAME, PART_NAM
E))
 
part.seedPart(size=GLOBAL_SEED_SIZE, deviationFactor=0.1, minSizeFactor=0.1)
 
target_edges = part.sets[EDGE_SET_NAME].edges
part.seedEdgeBySize(edges=target_edges, size=LOCAL_SEED_SIZE, deviationFactor=0.1, constrai
nt=C.FINER)
 
part.generateMesh()
 
num_elements = len(part.elements)
print("Meshed part '{}' with local refinement on '{}' -- {} elements generated".format(
    PART_NAME, EDGE_SET_NAME, num_elements
))

Source: abaqus_2024_scripting_reference.pdf
Page: 13

Notes / Caveats
PERSISTENCE: same as the global-mesh script -- add a final job.writeInput() once meshing is complete.
constraint=C.FINER only allows the local seed to make the mesh finer than the global seed at that edge, not
coarser.

8. Static General Step
Category: Steps
Description
Opens an existing model, creates a standard linear static analysis step with specified increment control, and
persists the result.
Prerequisites / Assumptions
INP_FILE_PATH must point to a valid, existing .inp file. PREVIOUS_STEP must already exist in that model
(typically "Initial", or an earlier named step).
Inputs Required

INP_FILE_PATH (str): Absolute path to the existing .inp file to open

WORKING_DIRECTORY (str): The task's working directory -- all output must land here, and nowhere else

MODEL_NAME (str): Name to assign the model reconstructed from the .inp

STEP_NAME (str): Name for the new step

PREVIOUS_STEP (str): Name of the step this one follows

INITIAL_INC (float): Initial increment size

MAX_INC (float): Maximum increment size

MIN_INC (float): Minimum increment size

MAX_NUM_INC (int): Maximum number of increments allowed

OUTPUT_JOB_NAME (str): Name used to write the updated model as OUTPUT_JOB_NAME.inp
Key API Objects / Methods Used
mdb.ModelFromInputFile(), model.StaticStep(), job.writeInput()

    raise ValueError(
        "OUTPUT_JOB_NAME ('{}.inp') matches the input file's name -- choose a "
        "distinct output name to avoid overwriting the original file.".format(OUTPUT_JOB_NA

9. Nonlinear Static Step with Increment Control
Category: Steps
Description
Opens an existing model and creates a static step with geometric nonlinearity enabled (nlgeom=ON) -- required
when large displacements/rotations or nonlinear buckling behavior are expected to matter.
Prerequisites / Assumptions
INP_FILE_PATH must point to a valid, existing .inp file. PREVIOUS_STEP must already exist.
Inputs Required

INP_FILE_PATH (str): Absolute path to the existing .inp file to open

WORKING_DIRECTORY (str): The task's working directory -- all output must land here, and nowhere else

MODEL_NAME (str): Name to assign the model reconstructed from the .inp

STEP_NAME (str): Name for the new step

PREVIOUS_STEP (str): Name of the step this one follows

INITIAL_INC (float): Initial increment size (typically smaller than a linear step)

MAX_INC (float): Maximum increment size

MIN_INC (float): Minimum increment size (typically smaller than a linear step)

Source: abaqus_2024_scripting_reference.pdf
Page: 16


